CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ready to quit smoking.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old patient presents motivated to quit smoking. Has been smoking since high school, starting experimentally with friends and at parties, progressing to daily use. Currently smoking 1.5 packs per day, with first cigarette within an hour of waking. Previously attempted to quit by going cold turkey and successfully abstained for almost a year, but relapsed due to work-related stress including layoffs and increased job responsibilities. Patient notes stress as a trigger for smoking relapse. Currently trying meditation and recently joined gym to help manage stress. Interested in using nicotine patch as a smoking cessation aid based on friends' successful experiences. Patient's motivation includes becoming a new father; baby expected any day. Chosen quit date is next Monday, which is also patient's birthday.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type two diabetes. History of gout. Systolic murmur noted on prior exams, to be monitored.

MEDICATIONS
Allopurinol.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Smoking history: 1.5 packs per day for approximately 26 years. No other tobacco products used. Recently started meditation and gym membership for stress management. Works full-time. About to become a father.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: Blood pressure 128/88, heart rate 68, respirations 16, oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, 2/6 systolic murmur appreciated (consistent with prior findings). Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally, no expiratory wheezes, no rales or rhonchi. Neck: No lymphadenopathy, no carotid bruits.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Nicotine dependence: Encouraged and congratulated patient on taking first steps to quit. Starting 21 mg nicotine patch on Monday (quit date). Patch location to be changed daily to avoid skin irritation. Plan to decrease patch dose over time. Follow-up in two weeks to reevaluate dosage. Continue exercise routine and meditation/yoga for stress management. Patient provided with handouts regarding common smoking triggers. Close monitoring of stress levels related to work and upcoming birth of daughter.
2. Type two diabetes: Continue management with diet and exercise. Hemoglobin A1c to be ordered for blood draw prior to follow-up visit in two weeks.
3. History of gout: Continue allopurinol. Continue to monitor foods that exacerbate uric acid levels.
